title: Browser-actuator verification: dedicated CDP profile, data-field consistency, honest partial results
summary: Failure+recovery lessons from LLM-driven browser-loop verification.
hint_triggers: Verification initially rejected: browser-actuator observe/decide/act ran, but the extension sidepanel execution path and a renderer data-field mismatch remained, so the original extension completion criteria were unmet. Recovery: fixed the data-field inconsistency, then ran fill_ref twice against a dedicated Chrome instance over CDP and confirmed both inputs landed in the composed preview — without touching the default Chrome profile or keychain. Transferable rules: (1) always verify browser actuation on an isolated Chrome/CDP profile so user state is never mutated; (2) a renderer data-field mismatch is a silent blocker for composed preview — check field bindings before blaming the actuator; (3) on partial verification, fix the in-scope defect, re-run the deterministic checks, and record the residual scope (e.g. profile-scoped Native Messaging, LLM computer loop) as an explicit follow-up with prior evidence rather than stretching 'done'.
